newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian Duma rejects 1997 budget draft.
newsitem.headline: Russian Duma rejects 1997 budget draft.

text.p: The State Duma lower house of parliament rejected the government's draft 1997 budget in a first reading on Friday by 280 votes to 33.

Deputies must now decide whether to order the government to present a new draft within 20 days, or to set up a conciliation commission with representatives from the Duma, the Federation Council upper house, and the government, to thrash out the differences.
The draft envisaged spending of 524.34 trillion roubles, revenues of 433.64 trillion and a deficit of 90.70 trillion, or 3.3 percent of GDP.
The lower house of parliament is dominated by the communist opponents to President Boris Yeltsin and the Duma's budget committee had recommended that the budget should be rejected.
Deputies were unhappy with the revenue side of the draft and said they had doubts about proposed levels of tax collection.

Revenues have been running well below budgeted levels this year, so the government has been unable to meet many of its spending commitments. Yeltsin on Friday created a special commission to improve tax collection and said government revenue had to rise so that overdue wages could be paid.
